findings.description: Critical: The frozen revision-2 consensus contract is a breaking replacement, not the additive migration promised by the plan. It removes the required reviewers array, replaces the flat quorum_met/quorum_requested/quorum_received fields with a quorum object, and removes legacy per-finding fields such as agreed_type and recommended_disposition. Existing consumers such as scripts/impl_review_driver.py still read agreed_type, yet no task or package migrates that consumer and the proposal labels only final-round convergence as breaking.
findings.resolution: Either retain the legacy top-level and per-finding fields as deprecated compatibility aliases for the revision-2 transition, or explicitly declare the report contract breaking and enumerate/migrate every reader, including scripts/impl_review_driver.py and impl_review_handoff.py. Add old-producer/new-consumer and new-producer/old-consumer fixtures before freezing the contract.

findings.description: Critical: The consensus contract can validate a false quorum signal: quorum has only requested, received, and an unconstrained met boolean, so documents such as requested=3, received=0, met=true validate. It also omits the configured minimum required reviewer count used by the convergence requirement, and does not constrain received to the distinct-vendor/request bound. This recreates the exact false-convergence class the change is intended to eliminate at the frozen trust boundary.
findings.resolution: Add the configured minimum_required value (or an equivalent immutable policy reference) to the quorum contract and define application invariants met == (received >= minimum_required), received <= requested, and received equals the count of distinct eligible terminal vendors. Add negative contract/application fixtures for false met, received greater than requested, and duplicate-vendor receipt.

findings.description: Critical: review-attempt.schema.json advertises a bounded attempt chain but does not validate the bound. An attempts array may contain unlimited corrective_redispatch and replacement_vendor entries, duplicate fallback-model attempts, duplicate/non-monotonic attempt_index values, arbitrary extra vendors, or a successful non-terminal attempt followed by a terminal failure and still satisfy the schema. The budget object merely records maxima and is not tied to the attempts.
findings.resolution: Enforce every expressible bound in JSON Schema (max one corrective and replacement attempt, exactly one initial attempt, and terminal success semantics) and add a named application validator for ordering, unique/monotonic indexes, configured fallback membership/deduplication, deadline, vendor transitions, and no attempts after success. Require all producers/consumers to call it and add negative fixtures for each currently-valid invalid chain.

findings.description: Nit: wp-consensus-policy owns and writes test_consensus_policy.py, but its only test command runs test_consensus_synthesizer.py. The package can therefore report consensus_tests_passed without executing the new pure blocker/adjudication policy tests required by task 1.4.
findings.resolution: Add skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/tests/test_consensus_policy.py to the wp-consensus-policy verification command and retain a result key that represents both suites.

findings.description: Optional: The 2 MiB limit is still specified only after parsing, so a CLI/SDK adapter can buffer and JSON-decode arbitrarily large output before the matcher rejects it. This bounds pairwise matching but not dispatcher memory or parse time.
findings.resolution: Apply a byte cap while capturing output and before JSON decoding, retain only bounded redacted diagnostics on overflow, and add an oversized-stream fixture; otherwise document the residual pre-parse resource risk.

findings.description: The revised plan correctly makes matching non-authoritative, preserves disposition per source finding, and explicitly prevents one replacement vendor from satisfying multiple round slots.
findings.resolution: Retain these fail-closed invariants and their regression scenarios during implementation.
